children: By Hina Navin

Dubai’s mortgage market is seeing a sharp rise in refinancing and equity-release activity, even as mortgage-backed property purchase volumes moderate from their 2025 highs, according to mortgage brokers and real estate consultants.

Sam Amidi, Sales Director of Mortgage Finder at Property Finder Group, told Zawya Projects that overall mortgage inquiries dipped in the second quarter by about 1.9 percent year-on-year (YoY) but approvals increased significantly, up about 33 percent YoY.

He attributed the higher approvals, despite growing buyer caution, to a shift towards refinancing and equity-release customers who are better informed about their borrowing position, as well as banks returning to more normal lending practices after a cautious period earlier in the year.
“Both of these factors contribute to higher conversion rates,” said Amidi. “Enquiries about refinancing and equity release grew 2.5 times year-on-year.”
He pointed out that around 95 percent of Mortgage Finder's enquiries come from UAE residents.
“First-time buyers make up around 80 percent of mortgage-backed purchases, with existing homeowners, investors, and other segments comprising the rest,” he said.
In the first half of 2026, mortgage loan sizes rose by about 17 percent YoY, largely due to higher property values, particularly for units nearing handover.
"Homeowners are leveraging the significant appreciation in property values to release equity, using it to finance renovations or reinvest in the property market," Amidi said.
Average deal size

Dhiren Gupta, Managing Director of 4C Mortgages Consultancy, said mortgage-backed purchase transactions across the UAE eased in the second quarter of 2026 and the moderation has continued into the third quarter-to-date compared to the peak levels recorded in 2025.

He noted that there were 8,822 mortgage-backed transactions worth 42.58 billion UAE dirhams ($11.6 billion) in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 13,604 transactions worth AED 42.2 billion ($11.49) a year earlier, indicating a decline of about 35 percent in transaction volume.
“Despite this drop in the number of transactions, the total value remained stable, suggesting an increase in the average deal size,” he said.
Third quarter -todate has seen 5,802 deals valued at AED 25.21 billion, down from over 7,100 deals worth AED 13 billion in the corresponding period of 2025.

“This pattern reflects a broader softening in transaction volumes across the market, even as underlying financing values suggest continued strength in average ticket sizes and buyer commitment at the higher end,” he said.
Brokerage deals

Rakesh Mirchandani, Co-Founder and CEO of RNR International Real Estate, said his firm received stronger mortgage-linked enquiries during the second and third quarters of 2026 compared with a year earlier.
“Roughly 40 percent of our ready-market closings now involve bank financing versus 30 percent a year ago, which is a 10 percent jump from last year,” he said.

He said 65-70 percent of the firm's financed transactions involve end-users, up from about 55 percent 18 months ago, while investors account for 30-35 percent compared to 45 percent for the same time period.
“Today’s mortgage landscape is decisively shaped by end-users—primarily salaried UAE residents - aged 30 to 45, purchasing long-term homes rather than speculative flips,” he observed.
First-time buyers made up 40-45 percent of RNR’s transaction records, upgraders accounting for 20-25 percent, and strategic investors comprising the remaining 30-35 percent.

“The vast majority of these financed deals (80-85 percent) are secured by UAE residents, while overseas buyers - constrained by tighter 50-60 percent loan-to-value (LTV) limits - make up the balance. Our registrations from May to August 2026 underline this trend, revealing strong financing demand for mid-market properties, including studios (AED 800,000–900,000), one-bedroom apartments (AED 1.3 million – 2.5 million), and family-oriented three-bedroom villas starting at AED 1.4 million.”
Mortgage activity rebounds

Citing Dubai REST data, Kunal Puri, Founder & CEO of La Capitale Group added that mortgage activity dropped to a low of 2,551 properties in May amid regional uncertainty, then rebounded to a peak of 4,402 in July as lender caution eased.

He said this rebound is driven by three clear factors: a sharp drop in fixed borrowing rates (now starting around 3.75 percent for a one-year fixed term), the success of the First Time Home Buyer Programme (generating over AED 5 billion in transaction value from 3,200+ buyers), and the June 2026 launch of Flexi Rent, which has freed up tenant cash flow for property deposits.
Refinancing trend

Haider Tuaima, Managing Director and Head of Real Estate, Valustrat said refinancing and mortgage top-ups made up about 50 percent of all home loans in the second quarter-to-date, up 15.9 percent on quarterly basis and 4.8 percent year on year basis, according to activity tracked by the firm.

“Apartments represented about 63 percent of mortgage transactions, while villas accounted for 30 percent,” he said. “This surge may reflect expectations of higher future interest rates, prompting homeowners to refinance and take advantage of their property equity.”

4C Mortgages Consultancy’s Gupta said the main driver for refinancing is the gap between mortgage rates borrowers face when earlier fixed-rate periods expire and the rates currently available on new fixed-rate buyout offers.

“As original two- to five-year promotional fixed rates expire, borrowers are suddenly facing variable rates tied to EIBOR, typically hovering between 5.25 percent and 6.25 percent. In stark contrast, a new, aggressive wave of fixed-rate buyout offers has driven rates down to between 3.79 percent and 4.39 percent - creating a spread wide enough to make switching highly lucrative,” he explained.
Rising property values are prompting cash-out refinancing - up to 75–80 percent LTV - for renovations or further investments, according to Gupta.

“For an AED1.5 million mortgage, refinancing from 5.5 percent to 4 percent could generate monthly savings of around AED1,200-AED1,500, allowing borrowers to recover switching costs within four to eight months,” he said.
RNR’s Mirchandani noted that borrowers who locked in peak rates in 2022–23 are now switching to save, with break-even costs usually under 18 months.
Central Bank regulations cap early settlement fees at 1 percent of the outstanding balance or AED 10,000, making the move relatively inexpensive.

“We estimate that 10–15 percent of our mortgage-related inquiries this year are about refinancing or buyouts, driven by rate differences, banks’ buyout campaigns, and homeowners accessing equity from appreciated properties,” he said.

Mirchandani gave the example of an RNR client, who refinanced his property and released AED 5 million at a fixed 4.69 per cent. The capital was then invested in ready units priced 10–20 percent below market value, yielding gross rental returns of 9–10 percent.

“The unit bought at 20 percent below market value can return 25 percent on the investment. If the market appreciates by an additional 20 percent, the total uplift could reach 35 to 50 percent, excluding rental income,” he concluded.
(Reporting by Hina Navin; Editing by Anoop Menon)
